A warm breeze sways drooping willow branches, stirring a slow gentle river, its wide banks home to long strands of cattails. Th ick 
clusters of lily pads with slow moving, wedge-shaped-shelled creatures quietly chewing, quietly chewing through them at a docile 
pace. Frogs and birds rest on this notably serene crustacean’s hard, flat shell while it roams the fresh waters, spearing all manner of 
river plants and chewing through the fi brous material with its long channel of teeth. Th ough blind, it has a highly developed sense of 
taste, able to detect the flora of its specialized diet and the flourishing surface algae. It is through the fi ltering and consumption of this 
scum that the ruske both cleanses the water ways for plants to proliferate, and develops its own inner toxins. Th ese toxins suffuse its 
body, giving its meat an impalpable taste and often lethal digestion, leading this creature to live a safe, if slow life.

River Born Th e ruske can breathe only underwater, and can 
survive outside of the water for a full hour before suffocating.
Peaceful Wader While the ruske remains motionless in natural 
bodies of water, it indistinguishable from the surrounding plant 
life and has Advantage on Stealth checks.
Languid Th e ruske has Disadvantage on Initiative rolls.

when creatures stand upon on them. Th e ruske can bear the

Encountering A common sight in many ponds and rivers,the 
ruske is often so covered in lily pads and algae growths that 
it is nearly imperceptible until it moves against the current. 
Tranquil to a fault, there is little that can alarm a ruske, and it 
will gladly carry larger creatures on its back while it peacefully 
munches through swamp scum and floating leaves.
Defensive Instinct (1/Day) When suffering a fatal blow, its slow, 
senseless reactions can keep it moving.
